Priya: Quick sprint summary — ran a 48h quant + warm-cache sweep on nova-11b (FP16 baseline) against a GTN-style slice (multi-turn help + longform). Goal: find the cost/quality sweet spot for default routing. TL;DR and mini-scorecard below, need product signoff on acceptable AVT delta.

Sam: what do you mean by AVT?

Priya: shorthand I used for this sprint: Answer Value per Token (AVT) = (helpful_rate * quality_score_adj) / cost_per_token. Helps reason about unit economics across configs. Not a replacement for qualitative evals, just a prioritization signal.

Luca: nice. can you paste the scorecard?

Priya: pasted. note: cost/tok is effective after batching, network overhead, and amortized KV cache savings. quality_score_adj is BLEU_adj weighted by human helpfulness on a 0-1 scale.

Priya: ```
Model | Config                 | cost/tok (USD) | p95 latency (ms) | AVT (norm=1.0 FP16)
nova-11b | FP16 (baseline)       | $0.00045       | 240              | 1.00
nova-11b | int8 static           | $0.00028       | 180              | 0.95
nova-11b | int6 QA-aware         | $0.00020       | 150              | 0.86
nova-11b-distill | FP16 distill   | $0.00030       | 170              | 0.78
```

Sam: int8 looks like the best marginal win: ~38% cost reduction, AVT drop only 5%. int6 is tempting for econ but AVT -14% and we saw more long-form truncation/hallucination cases in the sample.

Tara: did you break out short vs long sessions? GTN cares a lot about long-form quality.

Priya: yes — split by token-length: for sessions > 600 tokens AVT_int8 = 0.93 vs FP16, AVT_int6 = 0.80. hallucination rate (human-flagged) jumps x2 for int6 on >600 tokens.

Luca: what about KV warm-cache impact? many GTN flows have repeated context.

Sam: with prefix/KV warm-cache hit simulated at ~60% per session, effective p95 for int8 drops to ~120ms and effective cost/tok falls another ~10%. warm cache doesn't recover int6 hallucination though.

Maya: product question — what's our proposed rollout? default route to int8? or hybrid? we need target thresholds for acceptance (helpfulness / engagement delta).

Tara: my recommendation: default -> int8 (70%), FP16 baseline (20%) as a safety canary for long-form, distilled (10%) for cheap short queries where fidelity isn't critical. Monitor AVT and human-helpful-rate; require AVT >= 0.92 on GTN slice to keep >60% traffic.

Maya: sounds reasonable. for GTN we want no more than 1% absolute drop in helpful_rate and engagement lift improvement target >=1.5% (for any routing change to be net neutral/economically justified).

Kei: infra note — can add a routing flag `route.avt_threshold` and split policies by session_length. I'll add a feature flag so we can quickly revert.

ops-bot: deploy-canary: nova-11b-int8 -> us-west-dedicated-3 scheduled in 10m. Canary size=200 qps. Will post logs to /deploys/nova-int8-canary.

Priya: Action items (I'll take lead):
1) Roll out routing 70% int8 / 20% FP16 / 10% distill behind FF.
2) Add AVT metric and show per-slice (GTN_long, GTN_short) in console dashboards.
3) Start 48h micro-A/B (canary->ramp if AVT >= 0.92 and no P0 regressions).
4) Human QC sweep on 200 long sessions (focus hallucinations).

Sam: I'll attach the eval artifacts and notebook with the sampling/annotation script (link: http://git.internal/repo/nova-onboard/commit/3a9f2).

Maya: once canary runs, product will approve conditional ramp if engagement + helpfulness metrics hold. also want a quick FAQ for GTN to explain why we picked int8.

Priya: thanks all — will open PR with config and rollout playbook, and post back here with canary results in ~48h. :thumbsup:

Kei: added feature-flag `nova.default.routing` branch -> http://git.internal/repo/infra/branch/nova-routing-ff

Luca: thanks — nice concise decision.
